own_solution.law: Stefan–Boltzmann law: P = εσ4πr²T⁴. Therefore P2 = 1.5(10/5)²(1200/1000)⁴ = 12.4416 kW. A coating of thickness q cm on the second sphere gives P2(q) = 1.5((10+q)/5)²(1200/1000)⁴ kW.
assumptions: Both spheres radiate over their whole surface with the stated common constant emissivity.
Absorbed radiation is negligible, as stated.
The second sphere's quoted radius precedes the added layer, and its quoted temperature applies to the final outer surface.

notes: All certified answers agree with the radiation law. Coating thicknesses 2.5, 4.5 and 7.5 cm on the second sphere yield 19.44, 26.158464 and 38.1024 kW; the certified 26.1585 kW is correctly rounded. Coatings on the separate ball or disc leave the answer unchanged under the stated negligible-absorption assumption. Both explicitly claimed minimal pairs preserve the number, unit and tense while changing only the coated object. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag: pass 2 identifies the unquantified sentences as deliberate numeral-free controls, whose stated replacement relationship holds, rather than numerical minimal pairs. The governing relation correctly uses the updated radius according to the supplied wiring. The inferred emissivity is approximately 0.842, within its physical domain.
